statements.t: • In the second quarter of fiscal 2026, we recorded a $5.7 billion income tax benefit from the release of a valuation allowance that was established in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, as we now expect to realize substantially all of our existing federal deferred tax assets as a result of additional guidance issued on corporate alternative minimum tax (CAMT) by the U.S.
We expect to continue investing in key growth and diversification initiatives.
The following table summarizes the primary factors that caused our annual tax provision from continuing operations to differ from the expected income tax provision at the U.S. federal statutory rate.
As a result, we expected to be perpetually subject to CAMT and established a $5.7 billion valuation allowance on our federal deferred tax assets in fiscal 2025.
As a result, we no longer expect to be subject to CAMT in the foreseeable future, and therefore, we now expect to realize our existing federal deferred tax assets.
Changes in future taxable income, tax laws and other factors may change our determination regarding whether we will be able to realize our deferred tax assets.
As we look forward to the next several quarters:
• We expect current memory supply constraints and related pricing increases to adversely affect demand from several handset OEMs, which will negatively impact our financial results.
As a result, we continue to see increased product costs from certain of our key suppliers, which have and will continue to negatively impact our margins.
We expect the full benefit of these actions to be reflected in our gross margins in the second half of fiscal 2027.

• Beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, we expect Data Center revenue growth as shipments begin to ramp under our previously announced custom silicon agreements with certain large hyperscale customers.
• We expect continued intense competition, including from vertical integration by certain of our customers (for example, Apple and Samsung).

In particular, Apple currently uses its own internally developed modem in certain of its smartphones and we expect that Apple will primarily use its own modem products, rather than our products, in its devices going forward, which will have a significant negative impact on our QCT revenues, results of operations and cash flows.

Commitments and Contingencies.” Litigation is inherently uncertain, and, while we intend to continue to vigorously defend ourselves in such matters, the unfavorable resolution of one or more of these matters could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition or cash flows.

Our principal sources of liquidity are our existing cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, cash generated from operations and cash provided by our debt programs, which we believe will satisfy our working and other capital requirements for at least the next 12 months based on our current business plans.
We expect these provisions to continue to result in lower cash tax payments in future periods.
We expect to issue new debt in the future.

We currently intend to continue to use cash dividends as a means of returning capital to stockholders, subject to capital availability and our view that cash dividends are in the best interests of our stockholders, among other factors.

• Our purchase obligations at September 27, 2026, which primarily relate to purchase commitments with certain suppliers of our integrated circuit products, including those under multi-year capacity commitments, totaled $18.6 billion, of which, $13.8 billion is expected to be paid in the next 12 months.
We expect capital expenditures to increase from fiscal 2026 levels in the near term, primarily to support our engineering infrastructure and the testing of our integrated circuits.
• We expect to continue making strategic investments and acquisitions, the amounts of which could vary significantly.

We base our estimates on historical and anticipated results and trends and on various other assumptions that we believe are reasonable under the circumstances, including assumptions as to future events.

We monitor our investments, many of which are in early-stage companies, for events or circumstances that could indicate impairment, including, among other factors, lower valuations in recently completed and anticipated financings.

While we believe we have appropriate support for the positions we have taken or plan to take on our tax returns, we regularly assess the potential outcomes of examinations by taxing authorities in determining the adequacy of our provision for income taxes based on the technical merits of the position.

Factors considered in this determination include assessing the adequacy of future expected taxable income from all sources, including reversal of taxable temporary differences, forecasted operating earnings and available tax planning strategies, and considering that most of our income is taxed in the U.S., of which a significant portion qualifies for preferential treatment as FDDEI.

Changes in future taxable income (including less of our income qualifying for preferential treatment as FDDEI), tax laws (including changes to the CAMT rules) and other factors may change our determination regarding whether we will be able to realize our deferred tax assets.

However, we expect that certain companies may be dissatisfied with the need to pay reasonable royalties for the use of our technologies and not welcome the success of our licensing programs in enabling new, highly cost-effective competitors to their products.

We believe, based on our current business plan and the facts and factors known by us, our cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, our expected cash flow generated from operations and our expected financing activities will satisfy our working and other capital requirements for at least the next 12 months and thereafter for the foreseeable future.

statements.t: “We are pleased to deliver fourth quarter non-GAAP revenues at the high end of our guidance, along with 36% year-over-year growth in combined QCT Automotive and IoT revenues,” said Cristiano Amon, President and CEO of Qualcomm Incorporated.
Non-handset revenues are projected to grow by more than 60% year-over-year, and we are reiterating our fiscal 2027 Data Center revenue target of $5B.”
We anticipate the full benefit of these actions to be reflected in QCT gross margins in the second half of fiscal 2027.
(1) Our outlook does not include provisions for proposed tax law changes, future asset impairments or for pending legal matters, other than future legal amounts that are probable and estimable.
Accordingly, we only include such items in our financial outlook to the extent they are reasonably certain.
Our outlook includes the impact of any pending business combinations to the extent they are expected to close in the upcoming quarter.
(3) Our guidance for diluted EPS attributable to other items for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 is primarily related to acquisition-related items.

An audio replay will be available on our website and via telephone following the live call for 30 days thereafter.

We also exclude the operating results of acquired and/or consolidated businesses that, as of close, are expected or required to be sold.

Our Non-GAAP tax rate is determined annually based on our estimated annual GAAP income tax forecast (computed inclusive of both current and deferred income taxes), adjusted to account for items excluded from our Non-GAAP earnings before taxes as well as certain tax items that are unrelated to the fiscal year in which they are recorded.

We will periodically re-evaluate the appropriateness of our Non-GAAP tax rate and may adjust for significant changes, including significant changes in our geographic earnings mix, our corporate structure or tax laws.
